title: The human digestive system
description: Follow food from mouth to large intestine, then check what you remember.

cards.back: Waves of muscle contraction that push food along the digestive tract.
cards.hint: It happens in the oesophagus and the intestines.

cards.back: An enzyme in saliva that starts breaking starch down into sugars.
A liquid made by the liver and stored in the gallbladder that breaks fat into small droplets.
cards.hint: It emulsifies fat; it is not an enzyme.

cards.back: Tiny finger-like folds lining the small intestine that increase the surface area for absorption.
The thick, partly digested mixture of food and gastric juice that leaves the stomach.
A stomach enzyme that starts breaking proteins down into smaller peptides.

nodes.label: Digestive tract
nodes.note: The tube food travels through, about 9 metres long in an adult.

nodes.label: Mouth
nodes.note: Teeth chew food; saliva moistens it and starts starch digestion.

nodes.label: Oesophagus
nodes.note: Moves food to the stomach by peristalsis.

nodes.label: Stomach
nodes.note: Churns food with acid and pepsin to make chyme.

nodes.label: Small intestine
nodes.note: Where most digestion and absorption happen.

nodes.label: Accessory organs
nodes.note: Help digestion without food passing through them.

nodes.label: Gallbladder
nodes.note: Stores bile and releases it into the small intestine.

nodes.label: Pancreas
nodes.note: Releases enzymes for carbohydrates, proteins and fats.

nodes.label: Mechanical digestion
nodes.note: Breaking food into smaller pieces: chewing and churning.

nodes.label: Chemical digestion
nodes.note: Enzymes break large molecules into small ones.

nodes.label: Absorption
nodes.note: Small molecules pass into the blood, mostly through the villi.

activities.title: Organs and their jobs
activities.prompt: Match each organ to its main job.

pairs.right: Mixes food with acid and enzymes
Releases digestive enzymes into the small intestine

questions.prompt: Where does chemical digestion of starch begin?

options.rationale: Salivary amylase starts on starch while you chew.
The stomach starts protein digestion, not starch.
Starch digestion continues here, but it began earlier.

questions.prompt: Which of these are accessory organs? Choose all that apply.
questions.explanation: Accessory organs help digestion, but food never passes through them. Food does pass through the stomach.

options.text: Make bile that breaks down fats
Increase the surface area for absorption
Push food along the digestive tract

questions.explanation: More surface area means nutrients pass into the blood faster.

questions.prompt: Which enzyme starts protein digestion in the stomach?
questions.explanation: Pepsin works in the acidic stomach and breaks proteins into peptides.
Bile emulsifies fat so lipase has more surface to work on.

questions.prompt: Which organ's main job is to absorb water from the remaining waste?
questions.explanation: The small intestine absorbs most of the water you drink; the large intestine takes back much of what is left.

questions.prompt: Which are examples of mechanical digestion? Choose all that apply.
questions.explanation: Mechanical digestion breaks food into smaller pieces; enzymes are chemical digestion.
